objective: Proof. (i) Under flips and permutations of the three places the three-place knots form exactly five classes: parity, not-all-equal, the clause, the Fibonacci (no-lone) law and x or (y != z). (ii) Every knot other than not-all-equal allows a constant colouring, so on plain cubic systems only not-all-equal can fail. (iii) A law whose relations are unchanged by flipping every colour cannot pin a value, and among the knots only not-all-equal is such. (iv) Pinning theorem: if a signed law has a pinning piece, a relation that becomes an equality or disequality when one of its points is pinned, and a full (absorbing) piece, then deciding it on cubic systems is polynomially equivalent to deciding it with unbounded occurrences. (v) Schaefer status of the five laws. (vi) The clause cannot pin: a pinning piece would give an unsatisfiable cubic clause system, against Tovey's theorem.
status: Proved by PINNING-20261031-001A-P001: the 34 three-place knot relations form five classes (parity, Fibonacci, not-all-equal, x or (y != z), clause); only not-all-equal excludes both constants (the only knot that fails on plain cubic systems) and only signed not-all-equal is flip-invariant (cannot pin); pinning theorem: a pinning piece, an equality link and a full piece make cubic systems as hard as unbounded occurrences (NP-complete for the non-affine laws); only parity is Schaefer-tractable; the clause cannot pin (Tovey)
title: Five knots and the pinning theorem
